decision: User 2026-06-16: STOP the B=4 16-task deployment sweep, switch to B=1 temp-0.6 4-task per arm. B=1 (eff_conc=1, one codex task at a time, no co-residency) makes s/fwd_gpu directly comparable across tree shapes; B=4 does not.
why: At B=4 the prefill-independent s/fwd_gpu (per-forward) is CONCURRENCY-confounded: per-forward rises with co-residency (more query rows/forward, and the tree's rows = 9 nodes x B grow faster than native's 5 x B). During the B=4 run, cat9 was measured at Running:3-4 while native E5's whole-arm eff_conc was only 1.745, so the raw cat9-vs-native per-forward gap (1.23x) mixed a real per-forward difference with a co-residency mismatch (the same confound the morning data hit: 'E5 ran fuller yet faster'). The eff_conc-matched comparison was not determinable mid-run. B=1 removes the confound entirely.

b4_native_e5_baseline_archived.note: aggregate 20.12 = per_stream 11.53 x eff_conc 1.745; the ~2x gap vs fr9's 39.9 is the eff_conc term (concurrency-driven), not a per-stream regression. archived to output/.b4_deleted_*/.

b4_cat9_partial_archived.caveat: the ~18% behind was an UPPER BOUND: cat9 measured at higher co-residency than native's avg => concurrency-inflated. NOT a clean verdict. attention path = OUR forked FA2 tree-bias (FR13_FA2_TREE_BIAS=1 + _vllm_fa2_C.so), labeled TREE_ATTN by vLLM's backend slot; the per-forward delta is unattributed (more rows vs our FA2 fork vs tree-mask) and unconfirmed.
